items_missed: Never asked 'how are you today?' — went straight from the greeting into the date
Agenda statement was incomplete — said she'd take some information and walk through a customized estimate, but gave no rough time expectation

Never gave the customer a dollar total. Tanuja asked twice ('so if I take two end of August, how much do I charge?') and the call ended with only an hourly rate and an hours range — no total estimate was ever stated

No trip fee discussion at all on an Irving-to-Aubrey move with roughly an hour of drive time — she folded drive time into the hours but never addressed whether the destination falls outside the free service zone
On-Time Guarantee stated as a value ('ensures that we are valuing your time') but never explained the actual mechanic — that Einstein starts discounting if it misses the arrival window

No probe on garage, storage, balcony, or patio items; no special-considerations questions (long walks, narrow hallways, tight turns); no access/parking questions at an apartment complex or at a brand-new-build house
Never asked what she's worried about with the move
Washer/dryer and a 75-inch TV were logged as line items but never discussed as specialty handling — no disconnect/hookup or TV-box conversation, and no walk-distance question
Entire Save Your Ass prep speech skipped — no prep-shortens-the-move framing, no consolidation examples, no 'take a carload' tip
No booking attempt. She confirmed availability at the open, then when the customer said she'd talk to her husband, immediately went to 'I'll send you an email' with no attempt to hold the Monday date

Never mentioned the bolded detail list at the top of the email, never asked her to reply with corrections, never asked 'any other questions before I let you go?', never gave hours or how to reach the team
Never used the customer's name once, despite having her spell it out at the start
top_strength: The differentiator block was the strongest part of the call — she chained what's-included, no-hidden-fees, No Worries at $2,000 against the competitor's 60 cents per pound, Meet Your Mover, and the full clock explanation in one clean run. She also built real trust when Google couldn't find the new-build destination: 'I live up here in this area, I know exactly how to get in there.'
coaching_note: She never closed the loop on price — the customer asked for a total twice and never got one, which is almost certainly why the call ended in 'let me talk to my husband.' State the dollar range out loud (roughly $715-$920 at $204/hr for 3.5-4.5 hours), then ask for the Monday date, and settle the trip fee question for an Aubrey destination.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and affirming throughout, but 'thank you so much for that information' repeated verbatim close to a dozen times reads scripted, and she never once used the customer's name — the local-knowledge moment on the address was the only genuine spike of warmth.
